title: Counting bundles over function fields: Hall algebras, Kac polynomials and Higgs moduli
summary: Count geometrically indecomposable bundles on smooth projective curves over finite fields through nilpotent-pair groupoids and universal spherical Hall algebras. Compute the counts by partition residues, identify coprime stable canonical Higgs point counts, derive pure cohomology and nilpotent-cone formulas, and incorporate Mellit’s degree-independence theorem. General bundles, stacks, HN theory, curve arithmetic and plethystic foundations are imported from their existing owners.
readme:
This roadmap counts geometrically indecomposable vector bundles over finite-field curves and relates the count to partition residues, coprime stable canonical Higgs moduli and their cohomology. It follows Schiffmann's Annals 2016 article, with Mellit's 2020 degree-independence theorem and the Mozgovoy–Schiffmann all-characteristic count.

CB.0–CB.2 fix reciprocal Weil coordinates, automorphism-weighted groupoid masses and Jordan filtrations. CB.3–CB.6 compute these masses through the spherical Hall algebra and extract a finite residue formula. CB.7–CB.9 construct the canonical Higgs comparison and derive purity and nilpotent-cone formulas. CB.10 proves Laurent integrality and degree independence; CB.11 separates parabolic and HN refinements from the conjectural Euler-Hall Lie applications.

The geometric Frobenius convention pairs the parameters with product q. Hall multiplication places the quotient left and the subobject right; its twist uses v²=q. Ordinary differential residues and normalized Hall residues are distinguished. For coprime rank and degree, D=1+(g−1)r² is half the coarse Higgs dimension.

General bundles and quiver representations belong to their current upstream roadmaps; stacks, HN theory, curve arithmetic, formal-series machinery and monodromy are imported through their owners. Exact missing supplier interfaces and proof-closure gaps remain explicit, with no implementation claim. The authoritative target specification is the [reader](research/blueprint/readmes/CountingBundlesAndHallAlgebrasOfCurves.md), with its API and tests for every definition; the suggested Lean file is a compact arithmetic prototype over pinned carriers.

stages.title: Universal coefficients and bundle counts
stages.description: Specialize the existing reciprocal GSp torus and full character ring to curve Weil data, with an explicit genus-zero convention, and form K_g by inverting q^m−1. Define geometric-indecomposable counts and their HN truncations. Basic finiteness, rank-one, genus-zero, duality and periodicity theorems follow in CB.1, using a degree-one divisor rather than a rational point. Density is an explicitly requested universal-family input, not a new monodromy proof here.

stages.title: Coherent decompositions and finite-field descent
stages.description: Transfer finite-length module Krull–Schmidt to the additive subcategory generated by one coherent sheaf. Compute the endomorphism radical, nilpotent-to-unit ratio and finite-field Galois orbits. Establish the large-degree HN bound and the coprime absolute-indecomposability criterion. General bundle and HN definitions remain imports.

stages.title: Nilpotent pairs and Jordan fibre masses
stages.description: Define automorphism-weighted finite groupoid masses, nilpotent-pair groupoids, Jordan types, filtered-sheaf groupoids and the three grading functors. Prove the finite-field tower exponential identity and the Jordan-fibre Euler exponents. Fibre masses use homotopy fibres with chosen grading identifications.

stages.title: Curve Hall algebra and flag integration
stages.description: Construct the curve-specific completed Hall algebra, its exact-sequence product, extended coproduct and Green pairing. Fix quotient-left/subobject-right order, Euler powers and automorphism weights. Define characteristic functions and recover filtered-sheaf masses by pairing. Import Siegel and torsion-stack masses from their designated GS.0 owner.

stages.title: Eisenstein series and universal spherical form
stages.description: Define bundle, coherent and truncated Eisenstein series with their regional expansions. Prove Hecke commutation, coproduct, residue and HN identities. Construct the spherical subalgebra and its generic coefficient form, then descend flag, Jordan and truncated count formulas to K_g. Density supplies uniqueness; square-root normalization descent is an explicit proof obligation.

stages.title: Shuffle pairings and the Jordan sum
stages.description: Introduce the G and Y pairing series with exact variable order and expansion regions. Separate the torsion factor, compute the bilateral series and rank-one shuffle functions, and pass to arbitrary ranks by block residues. Sum Jordan types coefficientwise and identify the Young-diagram product. No unrestricted multiplication of bilateral distributions is used. Define the normalized partition residue kernels here, before their Jordan-product and generating-identity uses.

stages.title: Explicit residues and constant terms
stages.description: Use normalized and ordinary residues separately, and the J_λ,L_n,H_λ kernels on the imported Young diagrams. Establish the universal generating identity and the periodic residue extraction theorem, including genus-zero and elliptic rank-two checks. Prove regularity at the coordinate origin before defining the constant term, then derive its companion partition formula and the first four values.

stages.title: Canonical Higgs moduli and two-line charts
stages.description: Own canonical-twist Higgs (semi)stability, the stable GL_r coarse space and its proper Hitchin map. Import generic vector bundles from current AlgebraicVectorBundles, strong generation and Quot geometry from R09.2, and the routed good-line boundedness from ET.2b. Construct only the two-line framed charts, cotangent sequence and Kronecker embedding specific to this counting proof.

stages.title: Central deformation and stable Higgs counts
stages.description: Choose an explicit safe pair of framing dimensions, fix λ and King’s character, prove the moment-map indecomposability criterion and the stability comparison, and form the central-line GIT quotient. Prove smoothness, contraction and equality of zero/nonzero fibre point counts, yielding Schiffmann’s characteristic-bounded theorem. Add the Mozgovoy–Schiffmann Hall-integration route for the all-characteristic coprime count, with genus zero handled separately.

stages.title: Purity, cohomology and the nilpotent cone
stages.description: Derive pure compactly supported Higgs cohomology from the contracting symplectic action. Separate all-extension trace identities from weight arguments. State the signed compact Poincaré polynomial, reciprocal nilpotent-cone trace and component count with the corrected dimensions and Tate shifts. Spread out and compare to complex cohomology through explicit supplier contracts.

stages.title: Mellit integrality and degree independence
stages.description: Implement the curve-specific deformation of the partition kernel, with its normalization and variable exchange made explicit. Import modified Macdonald functions and admissibility closure through a requested continuation of the formal-series owner. Prove the z=1 cancellation and identify every degree count with a single Laurent polynomial; retain source-closure gaps for the generic combinatorial machinery.

stages.title: Parabolic counts and Hall-Lie questions
stages.description: Own the quasi-parabolic counting specialization, fixed-HN and slope-cut refinements, Euler-characteristic spherical Hall algebra and its primitive Lie algebra. Keep the stated parabolic R_g theorem distinct from the K_g argument available in the main source. Package the remaining positivity, HN and root-multiplicity questions as conjectural propositions, never as proved results or consequences of Mellit.
